text:
alex_w: quick spike idea — want to add a lightweight per-route 'differential-batching' config so the scheduler can choose a degradation path instead of a single fallthrough. thinking this helps avoid surprising quality drops for critical flows. :thinking:

maria_t: can you sketch the semantics? is this a control-plane-only hint or a contract the runtime must honor?

alex_w: contract. scheduler must be able to pick an ordered list of degradations and apply them atomically (if possible) until the request can be admitted. example degradations: prefix-KV-prefetch, microbatch->1, model-variant-fallback, and rate-limit-with-priority.

samir: sounds useful. my main worry: complexity of rollback when multiple requests in a batch have different allowed degradations. how do we keep batching deterministic?

alex_w: good point. proposal: degradations are expressed as an ordered vector of ops. scheduler tries the first op for the whole candidate batch; if admission fails, it tries the next op for the whole batch. we avoid per-request heterogeneity inside a single batch.

kenji: that makes batching simpler, but may over-degrade some requests. maybe we allow a "safe_merge" flag: when true, runtime can split offending requests into a secondary lane instead of applying degradation to the whole batch.

lisa: love the safe_merge flag. defaults should be conservative (i.e., avoid splitting by default) so we don't blow up tail latency with extra hops.

alex_w: agreed. default policy idea: prefer KV-prefetch and microbatching reduction before model fallback. fallback model is last resort. also include a short TTL for the applied degradation so we don't stick to low-quality paths forever.

maria_t: do we want to expose this whole vector to customers? or only a high-level knob (latency|cost|quality) and let the control plane emit the vector?

alex_w: recommend high-level knob in the public API and a control-plane expanded config. internal route manifest would store the explicit vector. public API: "degradation_profile": "latency" / "cost" / "quality" and optional overrides.

samir: RFC follow-up: need clear interface between scheduler and control plane. scheduler expects an ordered list of operations (strings) + parameters. control plane is responsible for validating model fallback compatibility and quantization expectations.

kenji: also reference telemetry keys: we need per-route counters: degradation_applied, degradation_level, degraded_batch_size. without that we won't understand user impact.

lisa: ops note — when degradation triggers model-fallback, we must log sample inputs to a quarantined s3 with PII scrubbing off by default. security needs opt-in for raw traces.

alex_w: quick config sketch (control-plane-expanded form):

```json
{
  "route": "/v1/chat",
  "differential_batching": {
    "profile": "latency",
    "vector": [
      {"op": "kv_prefetch", "params": {"max_age_ms": 200}},
      {"op": "microbatch_reduce", "params": {"target_batch": 1}},
      {"op": "model_fallback", "params": {"model": "redwood-small-q4"}},
      {"op": "priority_rate_limit", "params": {"level": "best_effort"}}
    ],
    "safe_merge": false,
    "ttl_seconds": 30
  }
}
```

alex_w: open questions: 1) should scheduler be allowed to mix degrade ops (e.g., kv_prefetch + per-request fallback) in the same attempt? 2) how do we express cost accounting when a batch is admitted under degradation?

maria_t: Q2 is big — we need to tag telemetry with "effective_unit_cost_multiplier" and make billing/backend show both nominal and effective costs. otherwise customers confused when degraded calls cost differently.

samir: Q1: prefer atomic-attempt semantics to keep admission logic simple. if customers want mixed strategies, they opt into safe_merge and split across lanes.

kenji: implementation plan: small runtime API tweak: scheduler->runtime admit(signature) becomes admit(signature, degradation_hint) where degradation_hint is the op vector index pointer. the runtime applies op transforms before admission attempt. minimal code change.

lisa: ops rollout plan: start with internal-only feature gate, collect telemetry for 2 weeks using synthetic pressure tests, then open to customers behind feature flag. plan for an escape hatch to disable fallback models per-tenant.

oncall-bot: Note: scheduled canary deploy on staging for differential-batching enabled routes at 2024-11-05T03:00UTC (job #542). :bell:

alex_w: thanks all — I'll draft an RFC follow-up capturing: semantics, control-plane API, runtime admit API change, telemetry keys, and rollout plan. ping @maria_t and @kenji for review when ready. :thumbsup:
